description: Repeat the configuration-write failure that leaves a node holding an unpersisted configuration, let the node commit that configuration, then restart it over the same log, stable store, snapshot store and transport and observe which configuration it re-derives. The admitted operation is the configuration attempt that failed; the result event reports the restarted node's latest and committed voter counts, their indexes, and the type of the log entry at the index it reports for its latest configuration. The check discriminates whether the configuration the restarted node reports is backed by a configuration entry in its log.

harness.description: Two in-memory nodes; node A's configuration write is failed once and it later commits the adopted configuration with the help of a fresh peer; node A is then shut down and a new Raft instance is created over the same stores, and the harness reports the re-derived configuration and the log entry at its index.
semantic_changes: one LogStore wrapper fails exactly one StoreLogs call; no target source is replaced
the restarted instance reuses the same LogStore, StableStore, SnapshotStore and transport as the original, with a fresh FSM
timeouts are shortened and the log level is raised to ERROR so the sequence completes quickly

legality.derivation: NewRaft restores the term and the last log, then scans every entry above the snapshot index through processConfigurationLogEntry, which is the only path that derives configuration state from an entry; it does not persist or restore the commit index. A restarted node therefore reports the configuration its log still encodes, which is why the restart is the decisive observation for whether the adopted configuration remains a configuration the node will act on.
legality.applicability: One node restarted over identical stores after it committed a configuration whose entry was never written; no fault is injected into the restart itself and the peer stays running.
unresolved: Whether a restarted node that still holds an applied FSM state inconsistent with the re-derived configuration is affected is not exercised.
alternatives: the ordinary restart of a node whose configuration entry is present in the log is not the discriminator

grounding.derivation: configurations.latest is the latest configuration in the log or snapshot and latestIndex is the index where it was written; a restarted node rebuilds that state by scanning its entries, so a configuration it reports after restart must be encoded by the entry at the reported index.
grounding.applicability: Applies to the restarted instance of the admitted scenario when it reports a two-voter latest configuration; the compared quantity is the kind of the entry stored at that configuration index.

observable_properties.description: If the restarted node reports the adopted two-voter configuration, the log entry at that configuration index must be a configuration entry.

uncertainties: The check observes one restart of one node; whether an FSM that already applied entries under the lost configuration is affected is a separate question.
